record.paper_title: Settling Some Open Problems on 2-Player Symmetric Nash Equilibria
record.original_question: For a two-player bimatrix game (A, B), where the rank of the game is defined to be rank(A + B), can a Nash equilibrium always be computed in polynomial time when rank(A + B) = 2, or is the rank-2 case computationally intractable?

evidence.quote: In 2005, Kannan and Theobald [9] defined the rank of a bimatrix game (A, B) to be rank(A+B).
Mehta left open the problem of determining the complexity of the following problems: finding a NE in a rank 2 game, and finding a symmetric NE in a symmetric game of rank 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (A, B) be a two-player bimatrix game, where A, B ∈ ℚ^{m×n} are the payoff matrices for the row player and the column player respectively. A Nash equilibrium of (A, B) is a pair of mixed strategies (x, y), with x ∈ Δ_m and y ∈ Δ_n (probability simplices), such that

  x^T A y ≥ (x')^T A y for all x' ∈ Δ_m, and
  x^T B y ≥ x^T B y' for all y' ∈ Δ_n.

Define the rank of the bimatrix game (A, B) to be rank(A + B). 

Determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given a bimatrix game (A, B) with rank(A + B) = 2, compute a Nash equilibrium of (A, B). Specifically, decide whether there exists an algorithm that, on input (A, B) with rank(A + B) = 2, outputs a Nash equilibrium in time polynomial in the bit-length of the input, or whether the problem is computationally intractable (e.g., PPAD-hard).
artifact.category_tag: algorithmic game theory / bimatrix Nash equilibria
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of computing a Nash equilibrium in rank-2 bimatrix games (where rank is defined as rank(A+B)) appears to remain open. Rank-1 was solved in polynomial time by Adsul, Garg, Mehta, Sohoni (2011). Mehta (2014/STOC) showed that bimatrix games of any constant rank ≥ 3 are PPAD-hard. The rank-2 case sits between these results and is, to current knowledge, unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Constant rank bimatrix games are PPAD-hard
status_evidence.snippet: Shows NE computation in bimatrix games with rank(A+B) ≥ 3 is PPAD-hard, leaving rank-2 unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Rank ≥ 3 is PPAD-hard; rank-2 remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fast Algorithms for Rank-1 Bimatrix Games
status_evidence.snippet: Adsul et al. answered the question affirmatively for rank-1 games, leaving rank-2 and beyond unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Rank-1 games admit polynomial-time NE computation; rank-2 status was left open.

status_evidence.title: Games of fixed rank: A hierarchy of bimatrix games
status_evidence.snippet: Kannan and Theobald defined the rank of a bimatrix game as rank(A+B) and gave an FPTAS for constant rank.
status_evidence.claim: Definition of game rank and FPTAS context.
